subject: Streaming billing: partial generations, disconnects, and retry semantics
messages:
From: Maggie Lin <maggie.lin@acmehealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Streaming billing: partial responses, disconnects, and retry semantics

Hi Neha / Jordan,

Quick question as we finalize our evaluation: your rate card lists token charges for streaming responses, but our concern is how partial generations and client disconnects are billed in practice. A few specific scenarios:

- If a user cancels mid-generation (client disconnect) but the server already emitted 40 tokens and the model would have produced 200 tokens total, do we pay for the 40 tokens only, or is there any additional rounding/overhead?
- If our client retries an in-progress request (due to network flakiness) and you receive two overlapping requests for the same prompt, how are retries metered? Is there any idempotency or session-level de-dup we can rely on?
- Are there special policies for partial outputs (e.g., if the model times out or is preempted)?

We also want to understand what baseline discounts look like for mid-market healthcare customers (expected monthly tokens ~ 200M). Can you share the hosted rate card and any standard tiered discounts?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that's easier.

— Maggie
Maggie Lin
Head of ML, Acme Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Maggie Lin <maggie.lin@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming billing: partial responses, disconnects, and retry semantics

Hi Maggie — thanks for the clear scenarios. I took a pass with the product and billing teams; summary + attached rate card and short FAQ. Attachment: Redwood-Ratecard-Q2-2026.pdf and streaming-metering-faq-2026.pdf.

Short answers up front:

- Client disconnects / mid-generation cancellations: you are billed for tokens actually emitted by the model (the characters/tokens that reached the client or were produced by the runtime). There is no additional "session rounding" that charges for the full max length. There is a small per-request header/handshake metering rounding that is accounted for as part of the request, but it is negligible vs token consumption.

- Overlapping retries: our hosted API treats each request as a distinct billed unit. We do not deduplicate across separate requests unless you use our idempotency key parameter on POST /v1/generate (or equivalent SDK param). If you provide the same idempotency key, only the first successful generation is charged; subsequent retries that match the key are not double-billed. Please note idempotency is best-effort for streaming workloads when the session is short-lived — we document edge cases in the attached FAQ.

- Preemptions/timeouts: tokens produced before the preemption are billed; partial outputs due to preemption are charged pro rata. When the runtime intentionally aborts work (for example, to respect a tenant SLA during overload), we surface that via response metadata so you can apply compensating credits if you desire — we can include a clause as part of a commercial agreement.

On discounts / packaging: our standard hosted rate card (attached) has volume tiers and a health vertical playbook. For the 200M tokens/month profile, typical commitments start at a 10–18% discount off public list depending on contract length (12 vs 24 months) and whether you need premium SLAs. We can be flexible on the first 60 days (trial credits) and will consider a one-time onboarding credit for streaming session performance testing.

If helpful, I can:
- Run a quick calculation using your sample traffic pattern (burstiness and median sequence lengths) to estimate effective $/1000 tokens after batching gains.
- Put together a draft 12-month commercial term sheet with proposed discount + onboarding credits.

Suggested next step: a 30-min call — Jordan can run model sizing and I can bring commercial terms. What does your calendar look like tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Streaming billing: partial responses, disconnects, and retry semantics

Hi Neha — appreciate the quick response and docs. Two procurement-y clarifications before we proceed to legal:

1) Idempotency keys: can you confirm the exact header/param name we should use in our SDK for streaming generate calls? We plan to use a client-generated UUID per user session, but we need to ensure the server honors it for streaming responses (not just non-streamed generation).

2) Can you confirm the accounting for retries where the retry occurs before the first response arrives vs after partial tokens are emitted? Example: user opens a connection, network blips, client retries immediately and second request returns the first 40 tokens while the first arrives a few seconds later — we want a reproducible rule to put in our procurement memo.

We also need an initial commercial concession: our board expects a 20% first-year discount for vendors in this category. We are open to a 12-month commitment and can trade an SLA uplift for additional discount if needed. Is there flexibility?

Thanks,
Acme Health Procurement Team

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@acmehealth.com, Maggie Lin <maggie.lin@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming billing: partial responses, disconnects, and retry semantics

Hi — answering the two procurement points and proposing a path to an agreement.

1) Idempotency header: use X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key on POST /v1/generate and include the same key for a retry attempt. Our SDKs (JS/Python/Go) expose this as the idempotency_key parameter on the client generate() call for both streaming and non-streaming. We will add a short code sample to the FAQ (attached) that matches your session-UUID plan.

2) Retry accounting rule (practical rule you can put in the memo):
- If a retry is submitted with the same idempotency key and the server previously accepted/started work for the key, only the first accepted execution is billed.
- If overlapping requests do not carry an idempotency key (or carry different keys), each execution that produces tokens is billed. In your exact example where two requests overlap and both return partial tokens, billing will include tokens produced by each execution. If you want deterministic single-charge semantics for flaky networks, use the idempotency key.

Commercial concession proposal: we can agree to a 20% discount on hosted list for year 1 with a 12-month committed minimum at your 200M token/month forecast, conditional on a short pilot acceptance criteria and a commitment to our standard SLA for Hosted API. Additionally, we will provide: 
- One-time onboarding credit equivalent to 5% of the first quarter's estimated spend to help with testing;
- A performance-verified burst policy during onboarding to validate latency at peak load.

Next steps: if that concession meets you halfway, I'll get a draft term sheet and SOW to your procurement and legal teams (DocuSign link included in hubspot deal). Otherwise we can pare back to 15% if you prefer a 24-month term.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to finalize. Proposed times: Wed 3:00–4:00pm ET or Thu 10:00–11:00am ET.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference
